newsitem.title: UK: Britain's queen must buy own helicopter - report.
newsitem.headline: Britain's queen must buy own helicopter - report.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government is planning to veto a defence ministry scheme to spend four million pounds ($6.7 million) on a new helicopter for Queen Elizabeth, a Sunday newspaper reported.

Finance minister Gordon Brown's anger at the scheme, which is thought to have gone out to competitive tender last week, reflects his impatience with defence ministry "foot-dragging" over his efforts to cut waste in public spending, the Sunday Telegraph said.

Treasury officials have identifed the Ministry of Defence as the "worst offender" among government departments which have been told to draw up a register of surplus assets by November so Brown can decide which to sell.
In an interview with the Sunday Telegraph, Brown said the national inventory of assets was a top priority.
"I have urged a speeding up of that so that no department can escape its responsibilities," he said.

Brown is believed to be particularly exasperated by the plan for a new royal helicopter because it runs counter to Labour plans to tear up proposals by the ousted Conservative government to spend 60 million pounds on a new royal yacht to replace the Britannia, now on its last tour of duty. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
